title: Nintendo Flipped an Entire Zelda Game Because Link Is a Lefty
hook:
Twilight Princess on Wii is a complete mirror image of the GameCube version, flipped in 2006 so left-handed Link could swing the Wii Remote right-handed. Did you ever notice Hyrule was backwards?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.

script: Did you know Nintendo flipped the entire world of The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess on the Wii? Every map, dungeon, and town is a mirror image of the GameCube version. Link had always swung his sword with his left hand. It was a Zelda tradition going back to the very first game in nineteen eighty six. Twilight Princess was built as a GameCube game, and that version kept Link left handed. Then Nintendo moved it to the Wii as a launch title with motion controls. Most players are right handed, and they swing the Wii Remote with their right hand. A lefty Link swinging the opposite way felt wrong. Shigeru Miyamoto wanted to change the controls without changing the game's content. So the team found a shortcut. They mirrored the whole game, left to right, and Link became right handed. Some staff objected, and the developers admitted they still got lost in the flipped world. The gamble paid off. Twilight Princess sold more than four hundred thousand copies in America that November, and most early Wii buyers picked it up. When Twilight Princess HD arrived in two thousand sixteen, Nintendo used the GameCube layout, and the mirrored Wii world became Hero Mode. Follow for more gaming history.
